entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # Madras (cloth). * Edit&action=edit "Edit this page [e]"). * View history&action=history "Past revisions of this page [h]"). **Madras** is a lightweight cotton fabric with typically patterned texture and tartan design, used primarily for summer clothing such as pants, shorts, lungi, dresses, and jackets. The fabric takes its name from the former name of the city of Chennai in India. [edit&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Definition")]. Authentic Madras comes from Chennai (Madras) in Tamil Nadu. Both sides of the cloth must bear the same pattern, and it must be handwoven (evidenced by the small flaws in the fabric). [edit&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]. Dutch traders arrived in India in the early 17th century to trade in the local calico cloth, followed by the British. [edit&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: National costumes")]. [edit&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Gallery")]. [edit&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: See also")]. [edit&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: References")].

entity_ranked_evidence.title: Madras, Oregon - Wikipedia
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # Madras, Oregon. City in Oregon, United States. **Madras** (/ˈmædrʌs/ *MAD-russ*) is a city in and the county seat of Jefferson County, Oregon, United States. Originally called "The Basin" after the circular valley the city is in, it is unclear whether Madras was named in 1903 for the cotton fabric called "Madras "Madras (cloth)")" that originated in the city of Madras (now Chennai) in Tamil Nadu, India, or the city itself. The name was rejected by the U.S. Postal Service over its similarity to a post office named Parmen"), and the name "Madras" was adopted, inspired by the cloth fabric "Madras (cloth)") of the same name, itself named for the city of Madras (now Chennai) in India. In the city, the population was spread out, with 33.1% under the age of 18, 10.6% from 18 to 24, 29.7% from 25 to 44, 16.1% from 45 to 64, and 10.5% who were 65 years of age or older.

Chennai,[d] also known as Madras[e] (its official name until 1996), is the capital and largest city of Tamil Nadu, the southernmost state of India. It is located on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal. According to the 2011 Indian census, Chennai is the sixth-most-populous city in India and forms the fourth-most-populous urban agglomeration. Incorporated in 1688, the Greater Chennai Corporation is the oldest municipal corporation in India and the second oldest in the world after London.
